python_example:
import requests
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# API Configuration
api_key = 'YOUR_API_KEY'
base_url = 'https://api.transitfm.io/v1'
headers = {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}'
}

# Work Order Data
work_order = {
    'title': 'HVAC Filter Replacement - Building A',
    'description': 'Replace main HVAC filter in Building A with MERV-13 rated filter. Check filter pressure drop gauge and document readings.',
    'facility_id': 'fac-789',
    'category': 'preventive',
    'priority': 'medium',
    'assigned_to_id': 'user-456',
    'estimated_hours': 1.5,
    'due_date': (datetime.now() + timedelta(days=7)).isoformat() + 'Z',
    'notes': 'Use MERV-13 filters. Building A main entrance lobby. Contact facility manager before starting work.'
}

# Create Work Order
response = requests.post(
    f'{base_url}/work-orders',
    headers=headers,
    json=work_order
)

if response.status_code == 201:
    created_wo = response.json()
    print(f'Work Order Created: {created_wo["id"]}')
    print(f'Status: {created_wo["status"]}')
    print(f'Assigned To: {created_wo["assigned_to"]["name"]}')
else:
    print(f'Error: {response.status_code}')
    print(response.json())
notes: Replace 'YOUR_API_KEY' with your actual API key from settings
Verify that the facility_id and assigned_to_id exist in your system
Use valid ISO 8601 format for due_date
Priority values: critical, high, medium, low
Status is automatically set to 'open' when creating a work order
Response includes the generated work order number (WO-YYYY-NNNNN format)
